requirements.md AC-024 (:794) nominally tests the approval boundary (Spec-Review-Status/Impl-Review-Status both read `Pending`, no `Approved`/`Passed` written), which would ordinarily satisfy this check. However, requirements.md's own Overview dated note (:47-55) asserts that Phase 2/3 activity — tasks.md, traceability.md authorship and review, and T-001 implementation-phase cross-model quality-gate verdicts (also relied on by AC-010, acceptance-tests.md:35) — already occurred for this same feature while that same Spec-Review-Status gate is still open in the current review round. A gate whose own governing document admits, in-band, that the work it is supposed to block has already happened is not a testable approval boundary: AC-024 checks only the literal string value of a status field, not whether design/build activity was actually withheld until approval, and the package provides no reconciling mechanism (no note explaining how a since-reverted or re-opened Spec-Review-Status is consistent with retained downstream artifacts). This is Critical per the calibration's "unsafe or unauthorized workflow boundary" class: it leaves the specification's central governance boundary unverifiable rather than merely under-specified.

The same phase-state conflict identified under CONTRADICTION (requirements.md:47-55 vs. :793-794 and acceptance-tests.md:18-22) leaves a design/task-decomposition reviewer unable to determine, from this package alone, whether `tasks.md`/`traceability.md` already exist with authoritative content that must be respected (per the dated note and AC-010's T-001 citation) or must be authored fresh from this spec, `Planned`-status, with no suite file existing yet (per Non-goals, Roles and Permissions :923-932, and acceptance-tests.md's own governing framing). A design reviewer forced to guess which of these two states is real would be inventing product/process behavior this package should have stated unambiguously — exactly the gap DOWNSTREAM-READINESS exists to catch, independent of whether the underlying claim is a genuine workflow violation or an authoring error in this specific document.
